title: Token-Level Uncertainty Estimation for LLM Reasoning
one_line_claim: Token-level Bayesian uncertainty estimation via low-rank weight perturbation identifies incorrect reasoning paths and detects hallucinations during LLM generation.
method_summary: TokUR applies low-rank weight perturbation to attention layer parameters, approximating the posterior over weights. Decomposes token-level uncertainty into aleatoric and epistemic components by sampling perturbed weights multiple times. Token-level uncertainties are aggregated to produce response-level predictions for hallucination detection.

key_findings.finding: Token-level epistemic uncertainty achieves AUROC 80.64% and AUPRC 56.79% on MATH500 for hallucination detection.
key_findings.quote: TokUR (TU) achieves an AUROC of 80.64% and an AUPRC of 56.79% on MATH500

key_findings.finding: Low-rank decomposition keeps original weights frozen while adding low-rank perturbation, avoiding fine-tuning.
key_findings.quote: Our low-rank adaptation approach avoids the need for model fine-tuning, keeping the original model weights frozen while adding a low-rank perturbation matrix

key_findings.finding: Response-level aggregation of token-level signals improves top-50% accuracy on reasoning benchmarks vs. response-level baselines.
key_findings.quote: Token-level aggregation achieves higher accuracy in identifying correct solutions compared to response-level baselines on GSM8K and MATH500

relation_to_herald.shared: Both operate at the token level during generation, extract per-token signals correlated with quality degradation, and use lightweight model-agnostic approaches.
differs_on: TokUR estimates uncertainty via Bayesian weight perturbation; HERALD predicts catastrophic failures from logit entropy and patterns under KV-cache compression.
TokUR targets reasoning correctness on math tasks; HERALD targets compression-specific failure modes under constrained memory budgets.
TokUR aggregates uncertainty to a quality score; HERALD produces a binary catastrophe prediction with configurable horizon lookahead.
